answer: A head crosses the bridge only by handing the keeper a fable reciting every head its maker was already granted, line by line; the keeper cuts the new mark into that maker's mirror, one plate per maker, opened once for that hand and never twice, and melts one bar of copper for every line the fable recites plus one for the new mark. A newcomer's fable recites nothing and melts one bar; a maker's thousandth head recites nine hundred and ninety-nine and melts a thousand, so a thousand heads cost five hundred thousand five hundred bars, all melted to slag.
